Body:
Operators $\scriptstyle \square$, $\scriptstyle \lozenge$ and $\scriptstyle \rightarrow$ are defined by: $\scriptstyle a\ \square\ b=\tfrac{a-b}{a+b}$; $\scriptstyle a\ \lozenge\ b=\tfrac{a+b}{a-b}$; $\scriptstyle a\rightarrow b=ab$.
Find the value of $\scriptstyle (66\ \square\ 6)\rightarrow(66\ \lozenge\ 6)$.
Explanation:
Given: $\scriptstyle a\ \square\ b=\tfrac{a-b}{a+b}$, $\scriptstyle a\ \lozenge\ b=\tfrac{a+b}{a-b}$ and $\scriptstyle a\rightarrow b=ab$, to be evaluated for $\scriptstyle a=66,\ b=6$.
Step 1: $\scriptstyle 66\ \square\ 6=\tfrac{66-6}{66+6}=\tfrac{60}{72}=\tfrac{5}{6}$.
Step 2: $\scriptstyle 66\ \lozenge\ 6=\tfrac{66+6}{66-6}=\tfrac{72}{60}=\tfrac{6}{5}$.
Step 3: apply $\scriptstyle \rightarrow$, which multiplies its two operands: $\scriptstyle \tfrac{5}{6}\rightarrow\tfrac{6}{5}=\tfrac{5}{6}\times\tfrac{6}{5}=1$.
Hence the correct option is (3).

Tip: Evaluate each bracket separately first. Here $\scriptstyle 66\ \square\ 6$ and $\scriptstyle 66\ \lozenge\ 6$ are reciprocals of each other, because swapping the numerator and denominator of $\scriptstyle \tfrac{a-b}{a+b}$ gives $\scriptstyle \tfrac{a+b}{a-b}$, so their product under $\scriptstyle \rightarrow$ is $\scriptstyle 1$ for any $\scriptstyle a\neq b$.
Subject: Numerical Ability
